subject: Re: Bounding boxes not tracking with video during review
text:
Angela! I saw your name and got so confused when I saw Mary CC'd in the
email because I was expecting your previous team haha!

Welcome on board to the Flock team - They're incredible and I am sure you
all will achieve great milestones together.

Thanks for the note - Encord works slightly differently to other platforms
where we are able to create, store & view labels on every single frame in a
video. In order to ensure there is the highest level of accuracy, we do not
downsample ahead of video-playback. Upon playback, this might be perceived
as lagging, but in fact is the computer rendering everything on the fly.

If you are interested in ensuring the overall accuracy, I would suggest
leveraging the frame-skip interval and using the keyboard to quickly look
at every 10/20/30-ish frames to ensure that the quality of all objects is
good.

Let me know how you get along, always happy to jump on a call.

subject: Sharing some information on DICOM metadata
text:
Hi team,

I hope you are well. I wanted to share some information about the metadata
pieces that Elena had raised on our previous calls related to displaying
the 'Series Description' for DICOM files.

Right now in Encord we have 2 types of metadata and we show both of them in
different ways and in different parts of the product.

   1. DICOM/file metadata - this is metadata that can be exposed in the
   label editor, there are certain fields that Encord requires and others we
   don't. If you pass the 'Series Description' here you should be able to see
   it in the label editor.
   2. Client/custom metadata - this is metadata that is custom and
   completely not optional, however it's super useful for filtering for files
   in Encord Index. If you pass the 'Series Description' here, you will be
   able to filter for certain ones within Index before creating datasets and
   projects.

A couple of things to note, client metadata can't be shown in the label
editor currently, and vice versa for the DICOM metadata in Index. Also
please note that Index has no DICOM visualization features, the only part
of the platform where you will be able to visualize DICOM files is within
the label editor when initiating a task.

I hope this helps answer all your questions but please let me know if
anything is still unclear and I'd be happy to help.

Seif
